# Syncing a Fork with Upstream While Preserving Your Changes

To sync your fork with the upstream repository while keeping your own changes, you'll need to follow these steps:

## 1. Add the Upstream Repository

First, make sure you have the upstream repository configured as a remote:

```bash
git remote add upstream https://github.com/original-owner/original-repository.git
```

You can verify your remotes with:

```bash
git remote -v
```

## 2. Fetch the Latest Changes from Upstream

Fetch all the branches and commits from the upstream repository:

```bash
git fetch upstream
```

## 3. Sync Your Fork While Preserving Your Changes

There are two main approaches:

### Option A: Merge Approach (Simpler)

```bash
# Make sure you're on your main branch
git checkout main

# Merge upstream changes into your local branch
git merge upstream/main
```

If there are conflicts, you'll need to resolve them manually.

### Option B: Rebase Approach (Cleaner History)

```bash
# Make sure you're on your main branch
git checkout main

# Rebase your changes on top of upstream changes
git rebase upstream/main
```

Rebasing rewrites history by placing your commits on top of the upstream commits. This creates a cleaner history but can be more complex if there are conflicts.

## 4. Push Your Updated Branch

After merging or rebasing, push your changes to your fork:

```bash
git push origin main
```

If you used rebase, you might need to force push:

```bash
git push --force-with-lease origin main
```

Be careful with force pushing as it rewrites history!

## 5. For Feature Branches

If you're working on feature branches:

```bash
# Update your main branch first
git checkout main
git fetch upstream
git merge upstream/main
git push origin main

# Then rebase your feature branch
git checkout feature-branch
git rebase main
```

## Best Practices for Twenty's Monorepo

Since Twenty is a monorepo using nx and yarn, you might want to:

1. Run `yarn install` after syncing to ensure dependencies are up to date
2. Run `yarn nx run-many --target=build --all` to rebuild all packages after a major sync
3. Check for any changes to the database schema and run migrations if needed
